newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields rise on French EMU worries.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields rise on French EMU worries.

text.p: Swedish bond yields were higher at midday on Tuesday, pushed upwards by worries that a French snap election might disrupt the timetable for Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).
"The whole EMU-project is at risk," a dealer said. "But the conservatives will most probably win."
Market players fear the French socialists as they have said they do not intend to cut back on expenses in 1997.
This means France would risk not meeting the convergence criteria that says a country's budget deficit cannot exceed three percent.
The six-month T-bill rate edged one basis point higher to 4.17 percent and the ten-year bond yield rose six basis points to 7.31 percent.
The crown strengthened to 4.4770 crowns to the mark versus 4.4875 crowns on Monday, helped by a stronger dollar and by the mark slipping somewhat after having firmed on EMU worries.
The Riksbank announced an unchanged 4.10 percent repurchase rate at its weekly Tuesday tender, which was in line with market expectations.
